label: GPT-6.1 Terra
output:
Hi Tolu, I’m actually in Biology 100L now and I wanted Medicine too, so I really understand why you’re confused.

Last year I scored 251 in JAMB and applied for Medicine and Surgery at a federal uni here in Lagos. When I checked my portal and saw Biology, I locked myself in my cousin’s room in Surulere and cried. I didn’t even eat that day. So please don’t feel like you’re overreacting because you’ve been crying. It’s hard when you’ve pictured yourself doing one thing and then you see something else on the portal.

My mum was still telling people in church that I was doing Medicine for like two months 😭 I had to beg her to stop. I know she probably meant well, but it was making it harder for me to accept what had happened.

Let me start with the transfer matter because I know that’s what you really want to know.

**Transfer to Medicine is real, at least in my school, but it is not automatic and it is not easy.** Our level adviser told us that to be considered for MBBS after 100L, you need a CGPA of at least 4.5 out of 5, and there must also be space in Medicine. So even if you get the CGPA, it doesn’t mean they must take you.

She also said that last year, about six people were moved in from the whole faculty, and she thinks over 40 people applied. I’m sharing what she told us, not saying I saw the actual list myself. But from that alone you can see why I wouldn’t advise anybody to accept Biology *just because* they think transfer is guaranteed.

She said you also need to have met the Medicine cut-offs in JAMB **and** post-UTME. I don’t know your school’s cut-offs or your post-UTME score, so I can’t tell you whether you qualify. Your 268 by itself doesn’t settle that question. Please check both requirements.

My own CGPA after first semester is 4.31, so I haven’t reached the 4.5. I’m still trying. That should also tell you that when people say “just read hard and transfer,” it’s not quite that simple. You can work hard and still find that the required CGPA is very competitive, and the space issue is there too.

Kingsley, I understand why you said transfer is a myth if nobody you know got in, but from what our adviser told us, people have transferred. So I wouldn’t call it a myth. And favour, I agree that staying home isn’t easy, but “just read hard” makes the transfer sound more straightforward than it is. I don’t think either answer gives Tolu the full picture.

**The most important thing is to ask your own school directly.** Our rules may not be the same as yours. Since your acceptance fee deadline is in the next two weeks, please go to the Biology department or faculty as soon as you can and ask them the exact rules. Ask what CGPA they require, whether you must have met the Medicine JAMB and post-UTME cut-offs, how they decide who gets a place, and whether there has actually been space for transfers recently. Don’t rely only on forum people, including me. If you can get the information from the people in charge before paying, that will help you make a decision with your eyes open.

As for what Biology 100L is like, we do BIO 101, CHM 101, PHY 101, MTH 101 and GST. Physics and maths are the ones really dealing with people in my set 😂 It’s not just reading about plants and animals the way some people think. You’ll need to put time into the other courses too, especially if you’re aiming for a high CGPA.

There are practical expenses as well. My lab coat was ₦6,500, dissecting kit was ₦9,000, and the practical manual was extra. Prices might be different in your school, but it’s something to ask about and plan for.

Now, is Biology a bad course? Honestly, no. I entered disappointed because my mind was on Medicine, but I’ve found things I actually enjoy. Genetics and cell biology are more interesting to me than I expected.

Our first BIO practical, we dissected toads. One guy in my group fainted 😭 I was fine, and that day I realised I actually like this thing. I didn’t expect to feel that way when I first saw Biology on my portal. That doesn’t mean you’ll automatically love it too, but I wouldn’t dismiss the course as bad just because it wasn’t your first choice.

At the same time, if Medicine is what you genuinely want, rewriting isn’t wrong. Just be honest with yourself about what another attempt could involve. My secondary school classmate Ifeoma rejected a Pharmacy offer because she wanted to rewrite for Medicine. She has written JAMB two more times and is still at home. I’m not saying that will happen to you, or that she made the wrong choice. I’m saying the “just stay home for one year and rewrite” advice can make it sound more certain than it is. Staying home can be difficult too.

Something else I had to think about, and maybe you can ask yourself privately: **do you want to study Medicine because it’s what you want to do, or is being called “doctor” something you feel you need for your parents?** It can be a bit of both, and you don’t have to answer anybody here. Just try to separate what you want from what everyone around you wants for you.

If you accept Biology, I think it helps to ask yourself whether you could give the course a real chance and continue with it if transfer doesn’t work out. And if you decide to rewrite, think about whether you’re ready for another attempt without a guarantee. Neither decision makes you a failure.

Please find out the rules at your school first, then take a little time to think about what *you* can live with. I know it feels very big right now—I felt the same way that day in Surulere—but whatever you choose, this is not the end of the world ❤️
